Final Text: ['When considering the effects of automation, it is essential to recognize the diverse perspectives on the subject. My perspective on automation revolves around the notion that creative work and knowledge-based tasks should not be replaced by machines, as it can lead to subpar results and hinder personal growth. While automation of manual and repetitive tasks may be reasonable, the potential job loss due to automation must be addressed to ensure individuals can lead fulfilling lives.', '', 'Comparing my perspective to the dystopian view, there is a common thread of concern about the loss of human elements in a world dominated by machines. With regards to creative work, my perspective aligns with the idea that some aspects of humanity are at risk of being diminished in a highly automated society.', '', 'In contrast, the utilitarian view and my perspective diverge in terms of the benefits of automation. While I acknowledge there can be value in automating repetitive tasks, the utilitarian perspective takes a less critical lens. The utilitarian perspective, as presented, concentrates on a very _theoretical_ model of how things work -- i.e., more things getting done quicker means more wealth and a better society. Unfortunately, that wealth is unlikely to be evenly distributed, and indeed, the people whose jobs are being automated are going to bear the brunt of the inequality.', '', "The progressive view takes a much more optimistic perspective on machines and creative work, highlighting the possibility that machines together with humans can push the boundaries of what's possible beyond what we can imagine. While I would agree in a theoretical sense, my view differs in that I am more cynical about what is actually produced through automation. That is, I am a bit more concerned that through automation we are simply facilitating the mass production of garbage. In reality the answer is probably both: automation allows for quick production of crap, but it also can likely be used in a thoughtful and meaningful way to improve the world. ", '', 'In closing, while automation can bring about efficiency and (theoretical) progress, it is crucial to consider the potential societal implications and ensure that individuals are not left behind in the pursuit of technological advancement. As we can observe today, the wealth from automation is not distributed equally. Ultimately, finding a balance between automation and human involvement is essential in shaping a future that values both efficiency and humanity. Unfortunately, we are not likely to easily find this balance in a capitalist system which devalues the latter :)', '']

Increased efficiency in machines means more reliance on them. With more reliance on machines, comes less human interaction. Think of all the movies that have been made where robots go rogue and take over the human world. The movie that comes to my mind when discussing automation is Wall-E. They rely on machines for everything and essentially have become a lazy society.  In the world of Wall-E everyone is living on a ship in space because we ruined our planet. They all rode around in motorized seats and just continued to eat. The Wall-E world with its animation is frightening. Fingers crossed that we don't end up that way.", '', 'I think my overall my perspective lies more in the Utilitarian and Progressive views. I would love for simple jobs to be made easier. I love being able to order on an app and directly note the changes and substitutions I would like. I feel this makes it more accurate and I am less likely to get tomatoes on my sandwich than if I told a human my order. But I also understand that by placing an order within an app has the potential to replace someones job. It is a balancing act between convenience and the people who previously worked the jobs. We need to think long and hard about the implications of advancements in automation and what that would do to our work force. We already have a fairly high unemployment rate, if we push out more self check outs, that takes away more jobs. Where do those people go to make a living? By cutting jobs, are we also increasing our debt as we are potentially having to give more assistance due to lack of jobs? Not every person is going to be able to go from assisting a customer checking out their groceries to a self check out repairperson.', '', '', "So I think we need to really think long and hard about what we want to automate so that we don't push things so far that we turn into the world of Wall-E. I am excited to see where things go as the advances we have made are extremely helpful. But I am not sure I am 100% sold on self-driving cars and trucks just yet."]

['Man versus machine is a long-standing debate. Historically, society has often grappled  with the implications of change as new technologies emerge. Throught the history of the United States and England, newspaper satirists have chronicaled the dissedent views and the fears surrounding the emerging technologies of their days. With the advent of AC/DC electricity, satirists claimed it was dangerous. With cellphones, some writers speculated they would cause cancer. Today, the speculations and fears continue to circulate as new technologies emerge.', '', 'With change, inevitably, comes loss and the unknown. The status quo, is lost when a technology changes the way society does something. For instance the status quo had been walking or taking horse back or horse-powered vehichles. That changed when cars began to impact the way people moved. With cars, we lost the status quo and we lost an the majority of commonplace horse ownership. When the car is first introduced, people sense the unknown depths of potential change. The possibility of change, the potential for loss, and the unknown extent to which these might occur make dissurptive technologies appear as a threat to those who are change adverse and sensitive to a fear of the unknown. ', '', 'To those who are less change adverse and to those who are less sensitive to a few of the unknown, technologies can perceived through a lens of potential. Most technologies are developed with the intent to do a good and helpful task.  For those who are unafraid, the promosing potential outweighs the potential for loss. ', '', 'With the advent of each new technology these potentials must be considered through a lens of logic rather than fear or hope. In fear, some have responded to the use of AI with a belief that artificial intellegence will cause humans to have fewer human-to-human interactions and, as such, the communications skills required for such interactions will diminish. Setting fear aside and reviewing this arguement logically, we can see the examples of ways that other technologies have already had a similar impact on a large portion of our population. For instance, social media and personal cellphones have diminished the upcoming generations interpersonal communication skills. ', '', 'However, to determine whether or not we can expect this outcome from AI and whether we can anticipate this outcome doing signficant harm to our society would require further research. Recognizing that potential exists is wise while proceeding with AI design. ', '', 'Personally, as someone who is neither change adverse nor sensitive to a fear of the unknown, I tend to approach AI with a different mindset. However, I recognize that my lack of fear is not always a good thing. Fear can provide healthy caution and can help someone prepare for eventualities that need they may need to be ready for. ', '', 'I would leap unknowningly into the future of machine learning and artificial intellegence unconcerned for the jobs that may be lost, the changes it may make on our society, or any unpredictable impact it may have. ', '', 'With an approach of embracing change, inventors forge a stronger, brighter, and more connected future, but they have also deepened social issues and cause problems they could not have foreseen. In the debate of man versus machine, neither the man nor the machine is the answer. Neither is enemy. The path forwards into a future where everyone can benefit is one where caution and concern are  balanced with eager anticipation of change. In this path, eventualities are considered, dangerous possibilities are mitigated, and hope is never stimied by fear. ']

['Automation, whether we like it or not, has become an integral part of our lives by offering convenience and efficiency in our everyday tasks. While it is often hailed as a sign of progress, the question of what is lost when we replace humans with machines looms large. We gain efficiency in our tasks, but what did we sacrifice for it? We now write much more, but at what quality? Perhaps we even use automation to cheat on schoolwork, but at what true cost? However, I believe in a different oppinion and, ultimately, reality. This paper aims to explore the notion that automation, especially through the use of AI technology, can serve as a catalyst for revealing and addressing our inherent inefficiencies in various aspects of our lives, particularly in communication and task completion. By examining the impact of automation on human behavior and productivity, we can gain new insights into the complexities of human-machine interactions and the role of technology in shaping our future. What we loose through automation, will only help us gain something better.', '', 'What do I personally believe? The answer is simple, through automation we loose everything that holds us back from being better. Need automation to do something 1000 times, why are you doing it 1000 times in the first place? Need AI to write your boilerplate english essay where you clearly know what the teacher wants you to write, whats even the point of the assignment? Require thousands of miles of conveyor belts and shipping lines to make peaches in Argentina, package them in Taiwan, and then ship them to Australia? Seriously? Do we not see a problem here??? So much automation is caused by our poor decision making and our short sided desire to make things work and have somebody else do it for us. When we have automation, we loose focus on how impotant efficiency is in the firt place, especially when we are concerned with global warming. Automation is just the next tool in our toolbox to fight the fluff in our lives and discover better ways of doing things. The less automation we need, the better off we are. The more automation we need, the more we need to reduce our workload.', '', '', "Automation exposes many flaws in the way we complete tasks, but thats not necessairly a bad thing. Let's look at a simple everyday task, your email inbox. Potentially overflowing with text you may employ automation to summarise emails and throw away junk emails. But think of the reverse side. You may use automation, such as AI, to expand emails to make them sound more professional to your boss. Your boss is just like you, and uses AI to shorten your AI expanded email. Now we don't have humans talking, we havee machines talking to eachother! But, don't get distopian, as AI has inheriently revealed a flaw we can fix. Instead of continuing the cycle, using more and more automation, why don't we allow the need for automation to expose what we can do faster. Why not just write shorter, more concise emails? Explain to your boss how expanding an email isnt professional, it's just a waste of time that would have required automation to fix! As we can see, by seeing how automation helps us reduce work, we can also see how automation exposes our own inefficiencies and use it to confront our shortcomings and strive for improvement.", '', "Another way automation, especially AI, is a good thing and aids in revealing inefficiencies is through the currently flawed hiring system. Have you recently tried to get a job/internship but turned down by terrible AI resume keyword scanners and flawed auto anylasis? Me too, and I'm angry. Lets consider why we are using automation. We are using AI and machines to automatically assess canidates on easily identifiable things in their resumes / personalities because we are too lazy to do it ourselves. Ok, well, why are we doing that in the first place? If the hiring process can be manipulated by simply adding keywords and answering personality quizzes, does automation really serve its intended purpose? All we've done is turn canidate selection from a battle of experience and ability to do the job into a neverending arms race of keyword optimization and personality quiz answer memorization. Automation is screaaming at us to reflect on just how inefficient our hiring process is. We need to cut out these issues and focus on what automation cant do, understanding the canidates ability to do the job through personal interviews and real world testing. We only started this arms race because there was a slight possibility somebody may get a better canidate if they added all this pre-screening, but that does not even matter anyways because its more likely the right canidate hasn't keyword optimised their resume and is instead improving their actual work skills!", '', 'Reflecting on the oppinions provided, my perspective mostly follows the progressive view. Both me and them agree that Intelligent machines challenge our long-standing ideas about what humans are or can be. We are personal beings meant to shape the world around us in meaningful and efficient ways, not drown in our own ineffieicy because of short sided goals or societial expectations. To be human is to challenge the order of things, not just sit around and hide all our ineffiencies under the methaporical rug of AI! Automation, in all forms, challenges the very way we do everything and the more automation does, the harder we need to reflect on whats wrong.', '', "In conclusion, automation sheds light on our inefficiencies and allows us to reflect and optimise. We don't loose anything bad from automation, only the fluff clogging up our lives that needed to be removed anyways. From the analysis of automation in communication processes to its effects on the labor market and the recruitment process, it is evident that automation challenges traditional practices and calls for a reevaluation of our approach to efficiency and decision-making. The Progressive perspective, advocating for the transformative potential of intelligent machines in redefining human capabilities, aligns with the argument presented in this essay regarding the need for reflection and adaptation in response to automation. By acknowledging the flaws and limitations revealed by automation, we are prompted to strive for greater self-awareness and critical thinking in utilizing technology to enhance our lives. Rather than succumbing to the allure of automated solutions, it is essential to recognize the opportunities for growth and innovation that arise from the exposure of inefficiencies. Embracing the challenges posed by automation and actively engaging with the implications of technological advancements can lead to a more informed and proactive approach to shaping a more efficient and human-centric society. As we continue to navigate the complexities of a rapidly evolving technological landscape, the ability to utilize automation as a tool for introspection and improvement will be crucial in fostering progress and resilience in the face of societal challenges.", '']

['Automation is often heralded as a marker of societal progress, yet it raises the important question of what is forfeited when humans are supplanted by machines. The erosion of basic courtesies, respect, and genuine interpersonal connections in our daily exchanges is a consequence of relying on intelligent machines for various tasks, potentially leading to a disconnect from fundamental social values. Additionally, the diminishing passion and emotion that come with human interaction may be lost in the transactional nature of relationships with automated systems.', '', 'Conversely, the utilitarian view argues that machines excel at monotonous, repetitive tasks and precise, high-speed functions, surpassing humans in efficiency. This efficiency is believed to contribute to the prosperity and advancement of society, benefiting individuals in the long term. However, this efficiency may come at the cost of the passion and creativity that humans bring to their work.', '', 'The progressive standpoint suggests that the advent of intelligent machines challenges traditional concepts of human potential, pushing both humans and machines towards uncharted possibilities. This perspective recognizes the transformative impact of automation on our understanding of humanity and the evolving relationship between humans and technology.', '', 'My perspective aligns with a balance of the utilitarian and progressive views, acknowledging the potential for automation to enhance productivity and innovation in society while also recognizing the risks of losing essential human qualities and passion in the process. ['\tAs human beings, we strive to continue progressing toward a better future. Automation has been at the forefront of this ongoing progress, impacting numerous industries and sectors worldwide. From manufacturing and transportation to healthcare and finance. Automation technology has revolutionized the way we work, live, and play. But at what cost? Are we, as a society, losing our connection to one another? Humans are social beings who thrive on connections and relationships with others. While automation and technology have greatly enhanced our efficiency and productivity, they cannot replace the emotional and psychological benefits that come from human interaction. Machines cannot replace humans.', "    The Utilitarian view that machines are faster and more efficient than humans is not wrong, When it comes to manufacturing, many jobs that involve routine, predictable tasks have been replaced by machines. These include tasks such as assembly line work, material handling, packaging, and quality control. Machines can perform these tasks faster, more accurately, and with fewer errors compared to human workers, leading to increased productivity and cost savings for companies. Being as manufacturing is not a customer facing industry, machines don't have as big of an impact on society. However, in industries such as customer service, where face to face interactions can make or break the potential return of customers, robots have more of an impact on society.", '    On one hand, automation in customer service has led to faster response times, 24/7 availability, and personalized interactions through chatbots, virtual assistants, and self-service portals. This has enhanced the overall customer experience by providing instant support, resolving queries quickly, and offering convenient access to information and services. there are concerns about the loss of human touch and empathy in customer interactions when companies rely too heavily on automated systems. While automation can provide quick and efficient responses, it may lack the emotional intelligence, understanding, and personalization that human agents bring to customer service engagements. To address these challenges, companies must strike a balance between automation and human interaction in their customer service operations. By leveraging automation to handle routine tasks and providing human agents for more complex and sensitive interactions, businesses can deliver a personalized, efficient, and empathetic customer experience that meets the diverse needs of customers while supporting the well-being of the workforce.', '']

['If factory processes are automated, products can be made more quickly and at a lower price, which boosts economic growth. This economic growth in turn can allow for more free time which people can use to spend time with other people. Many human jobs being replaced by robots are tedious and easy to automate. They tend not to require skills unique to humans; if they did, they couldn\'t be automated. Replacing humans with machines in these circumstances allows for the humans to have careers that they might find more fulfilling and less tedious. Thus I agree with the "Utilitarian View."', '', 'However, we must be vigilant as a society to not become so overrun with machinery that we stop interacting with humans to the degree we do now. There are many qualities of human thought that cannot be replicated by current technology; creativity is a good example, as current AI focuses only on ideas that have already existed (and been fed into their models). It is this creativity and a hunger for new ideas which allows human society to flourish and advance. Also, just as our bodies need to constantly exercise to stay in shape, so too must humans engage their social skills frequently so that they do not erode. Humans are social creatures, and it would be detrimental if humans are replaced by machines for companionship. If they are, then humans will become less kind to each other—there is no need to be kind to a machine, since it obeys no matter what—and socializing will become less satisfying. At the very worst, people could become confrontational and violence could break out at a greatly increased rate. For these reasons, I also agree with the "Dystopian View" in that machines should not replace humans as companions to other humans. However, it is perfectly fine for machines to replace humans as the guts doing unskilled and tedious work—in fact, this will allow for more leisure and a more prosperous society.']

The displacement of workers in various industries raises questions about how individuals will sustain themselves financially in the future.', '', 'Furthermore, the erosion of respect in daily interactions is a concerning trend resulting from decreased human contact. As people increasingly turn to online platforms for communication, there is a noticeable decline in empathy and tolerance in face-to-face interactions. This shift towards a more self-centered mentality is exacerbated by the removal of human elements from everyday activities.', '', 'Moreover, the evolution of technology has not progressed as smoothly as anticipated, with frequent system glitches and aggravating processes causing frustration for users. ['Automation is an extension of the industrial age of machinery, taken to unforseen dimensions. Nevertheless, machine automation has great potentialities to elevate the human race and even become like a parent-child relationship, with the child (i.e. AI) grown into a postive partner with humans. ['I believe that humans being replaced by machines for some jobs is amazing because of the fact that it stops humans from getting hurt doing some of the tasks that machines can easily do. To work off of the example about assembly lines being supported by robots now instead of using humans, there were definitely benefits there for humans. For example, robots are designed to perform repetitive tasks at a time with a much better endurance than a human can so replacing the humans with robots stops injuries from repetitive motions such as strains and sprains. Robots can also operate the sharp tools and equipment that humans would normally use in the assembly lines which prevents cuts and scars from humans accidently misusing those tools. Lastly, replacing humans with machines helps prevent the many respiratory issues that occur when working in the assembly lines due to the exposure to dust, fumes, or other airborne particles. Overall, replacing humans with machines in assembly lines and other similar types of jobs that are low-skill, repetitive jobs are the type of jobs that should be automated.', '', 'However, while I agree with the utilitarian view in some aspects, I also agree with the dystopian view in the cases that are appearing a lot today. In recent times, there has been an explosion of using robots to automate jobs like cashiers, waiters, and baristas. I completely disagree with using robots to automate jobs like these because these are jobs that lose their human touch when they are replaced by machines. Although I see the convinence in having automated stations for people to order their drinks or check out their items for themselves, that should not be happening at the expense of valuable entry-level jobs that people need in order to establish themselves in the economy. Similarly, I believe that robots should be used to replace some corporate jobs as well such as software engineering and design oriented jobs because although these chatbots have shown their prowless in writing code and creating art, these types of jobs need a human touch for their products to be successful. No matter how much robots improve, until they can truly think like how humans can, I do not believe that we should let them design anything because one of the greatest gifts that humanity has is our boundless imagination.', '', 'Overall, I believe that my perspective on replacing humans with machines does not align with one single perspective but with a mix between the dystopian and the utilitarian perspectives. I want humans to not get hurt as much from the jobs that place them in highly harmful work environments but I also believe that robots should not replace some jobs that require a human touch. I hope that moving forward, people realize that there are some jobs that can be replaced but not every single job can be replaced by machines.']

['As automation continues to increase in various industries, the debate over the implications of replacing humans with machines becomes more important than ever. While many argue that automation is a sign of progress and leads to greater efficiency, others view it as a threat to our humanity and interpersonal connections. The question remains: what do we lose when intelligent machines take over tasks once performed by humans? My position on the issue of replacing humans with machines in various industries is mostly utilitarian but with some limitations. While I acknowledge the benefits of automation in terms of efficiency and productivity, I also recognize the importance of maintaining human connections through the avenue of work.', '', 'From a utilitarian standpoint, the use of intelligent machines in repetitive and precise tasks undoubtedly leads to increased productivity and economic growth. It allows for faster production, higher quality goods, and ultimately a more prosperous world for everyone. However, solely focusing on efficiency and output can sometimes neglect the human aspect of work and life. While automation can streamline processes and boost productivity, it is crucial to not lose sight of the importance of human interaction, empathy, and relationships. Automation should be a tool to enhance our lives and work, rather than replace the value of human connection and understanding. An excess application of the utilitarian view could cause a societal state that resembles the dystopian perspective, wherein complete automation of labor causes people to become so isolated and unsure about their place in the world that we experience a sort of social degeneration that manifests through widespread disorder. By integrating intelligent machines into our society while emphasizing the importance of human values, we can create a future that combines the best of both worlds.', '', 'In analyzing the relationship between my perspective and the utilitarian view, I see the complementary nature of both. While the utilitarian perspective focuses on the tangible benefits of automation in terms of productivity and economic growth, my viewpoint adds the dimension of human values and connections. By considering both efficiency and humanity in decision-making and implementation of automation, we can strive to create a balanced and sustainable future where both humans and machines coexist harmoniously.']

['\tWhen considering the issue of automation, the main point of contention is the amount of automation that can be implemented without significantly undermining individuals\' lives. Perspectives on this issue are largely determined by what each person considers "significant". Some draw the line at automation decreasing the positions available in an industry (i.e. "robots are taking peoples\' jobs") while others recognize the benefits of automation while maintaining skepticism of artificial intelligence such as ChatGPT. Personally, I recognize that the efficiency automation brings enables the lifestyle that I currently enjoy and do not consider automation in areas where human participation is objectively less efficient to be particulary egregious. Though I recognize the merits of the "Dystopian view" as the logic appears to be sound, my own opinion differs considering my social anxiety. The rise of automation in traditionally human-dependent fields, such as customer service, may benefit those who struggle with communication, despite potential drawbacks for those who do not. In other words, the issue of automation can never be "solved" per se as each individual\'s perspective has merit. Put simply, the line is drawn based on one\'s priorities, my perspective prioritizes my comfort whereas the "dystopian" view prioritizes society\'s communication.']

['My perspective on the issue of automation replacing humans is that it is a complex and multifaceted issue. While automation can certainly bring about increased efficiency and productivity, it also raises concerns about the impact on human workers and society as a whole. ', '', 'From the perspective of intelligent machines, the argument is made that they are better suited for certain tasks than humans, leading to a more prosperous and progressive world. This utilitarian view focuses on the benefits of automation in terms of increased efficiency and productivity, which can ultimately lead to economic growth and advancement. However, this perspective fails to consider the implications of widespread automation on the human workforce and the potential social consequences of mass unemployment and income inequality.', '', 'On the other hand, the dystopian view highlights the loss of human connection and empathy that comes with the replacement of people by machines. When our daily interactions are with machines rather than with other human beings, we risk losing touch with our own humanity and the value of interpersonal relationships. This perspective emphasizes the importance of preserving human-centric values and experiences in a world increasingly dominated by technology.', '', 'Lastly, the progressive view sees intelligent machines as a catalyst for pushing both humans and machines towards new possibilities. While automation may challenge traditional notions of what it means to be human, it also presents opportunities for innovation and growth. This perspective recognizes the potential for collaboration between humans and machines to create a more advanced and dynamic society.', '', 'In conclusion, my perspective on automation is that it is essential to consider the balance between the benefits of efficiency and productivity that come with intelligent machines, and the potential consequences for human workers and society. It is important to approach automation thoughtfully and ethically, taking into account the impact on individuals and communities, while also embracing the opportunities for progress and innovation that automation can bring.']

', '', 'An argument against automation is the fear of job loss and unemployment rates spiking. ['The usage of artificial intelligence has increased over the years, with programs like ChatGPT and others forming new ways to enhance or even replace human work. To give an example, machines used in factories have progressed industrialization and even improved working conditions for factory workers. On the other hand, if machines were to be in replacement for positions that require human interaction like professional athletes, therapists, teachers or even detectives; I believe it would do more damage than good. There are things that are limited to human abilities and there are things that should be left for machines to do. Machines cannot have human emotions and it would be hard to replicate them. Using machines in situations that deal with morality and empathy would only cause the machine to respond with logic. Nowadays, AI is being used for things that were for human enjoyment like art so that it could be profitable. AI is also used academically which can be both good and bad. The use of AI can be beneficial when it is used as an aid and not as a replacement.', "When comparing my perspective to anothers, I would say that my opinion would fall in between the dystopian view and the utilitarian view. I can see why one would think that replacing people with machines would cause us to lose our humanity. It can be thought of as a sci-fi situation where robots replace humans completely. Although it doesn't seem possible for androids to replace us in the near future, it is also a reoccuring thought that machines will soon replace job positions where humans were once working in. I think that if people see more machines replacing job positions, the workload will become more demanding to keep up with the machine - it'll overwork the human employee. In return, this could lead to people having less respect and tolerance from others as stated in the dystopian view.", 'As for the utilitarian view, I agree with the thought that machines are good at low-skill repetitive jobs. This is why it was beneficial in factories and in mass production. It was able to help speed up the process of creating and selling when there is high demand for the product. I believe that before there were machines to do these tasks, there would be people working in unsafe conditions to make sure that these products were sold as fast as possible. Although, this issue is still prevalent now in sweat shops. Efficiency is important in sales and machines did make the process way more efficient.', "To conclude with, intelligent machines have the potential to replace humans and leave it lasting effects but if we were to consistently regulate our usage with machines as a way to only aid our ideas, then it won't get to the point of replacment. It's important to educate others of the consequences of using AI as well as creating technology that is relied on humans instead of the other way around."]

['The discourse surrounding the impact of automation on society is a multifaceted one, encapsulating contrasting viewpoints that provide a nuanced understanding of the consequences of replacing human labor with machines. Two prominent perspectives, namely the Utilitarian and Dystopian views, offer compelling insights into the implications of this technological shift.', '', 'From a Utilitarian standpoint, the advantages of automation are underscored by its ability to enhance operational efficiency and drive economic progress. Machines excel in executing repetitive tasks with precision and speed, leading to increased productivity and innovation across various industries. By optimizing processes through automation, organizations can achieve higher levels of output and competitiveness in an ever-evolving market landscape. The Utilitarian view champions the tangible benefits of automation in bolstering efficiency and propelling societal advancement.', '', 'Conversely, the Dystopian perspective raises valid concerns regarding the potential erosion of human connection and empathy in a world increasingly dominated by intelligent machines. The apprehension centers on the risk of devaluing interpersonal relationships and diminishing the intrinsic qualities that define our humanity. As automation encroaches on tasks that necessitate emotional intelligence and creativity, there is a palpable apprehension surrounding the loss of human touch and its implications for social cohesion. The Dystopian view underscores the significance of preserving the nuances of human interaction amidst the proliferation of automation.', '', 'The juxtaposition of the Utilitarian and Dystopian views underscores the intricate balance between reaping the benefits of automation and safeguarding the quintessential aspects of human experience. As societies navigate the complexities of integrating intelligent machines into various facets of everyday life, a nuanced approach that acknowledges both the efficiencies of automation and the significance of human connection is imperative. Striking a harmonious equilibrium between leveraging technology for progress and upholding the value of empathy and interpersonal relationships is paramount in charting a sustainable path forward in an increasingly automated world.', '', 'By acknowledging the divergent perspectives of the Utilitarian and Dystopian views on automation, we gain a holistic understanding of the challenges and opportunities presented by technological advancements. Embracing this duality enables us to navigate the evolving landscape of automation with wisdom and foresight, ensuring that the integration of intelligent machines aligns with our collective values and aspirations for a harmonious coexistence between humans and technology']

['Automation: "The use of machines, technology, and software to perform tasks that were previously carried out by humans. In the context of replacing human jobs, automation involves the implementation of systems that can perform tasks more efficiently, accurately, and cost-effectively than humans. This can result in job losses as tasks are automated and the need for human labor decreases." ', 'Automation is a big issue nowadays, as AI is becoming increasingly popular, and models such as ChatGPT are assisting people with a variety of tasks, both personal and professional. These AI large language models are efficient and helpful, at least on the surface level. There are a variety of different perspectives regarding automation, illustrated by the dystopian, utilitarian, and progressive viewpoints of automation. ', 'The dystopian view of automation considers the humanity of automation, arguing that we would lose our humanity by replacing people with machines. The utilitarian view of automation considers how efficient automation is and how helpful that would be in the workplace for humans being extremely precise and high-speed. The progressive view argues that automation is a form of progress, allowing us to challenge our long-standing ideas and beliefs about what humans are or can be, ultimately pushing us towards possible unrealized potential.', "Personally, I can understand many of the arguments both for and against automation.  As a business major in college, I understand the potential business-based benefits that automation offers: reduced costs (because an AI LLM doesn't need to be paid for work it produces, unlike a human... but could this cross over into some ethical implications?), safety (reducing human risks by allowing AI to take over the more dangerous aspects of a job), etc. I also can see the potential drawbacks such as the idea of an AI taking over jobs - this is a real concern for jobs that humans may not necessarily need to do (such as accounting, or copywriting). These concerns are valid and real, for both employees and employers. ", "Honestly, I can't say that I'm necessarily for or against automation. I think there are positives and negatives, both yet to be discovered. I can't align my own views with one view provided in the prompt, however I am going into this new, largely uncharted territory with an open mind. I think we will experience a lot of positives, and some negatives throughout this journey.", "I think that I most closely align with the progressive view, which differs vastly from the dystopian view. I'm not automatically assuming that we will lose all humanity when automation becomes more popular. I think there will be positives and negatives to come. "]

["\tHumanity has never been afraid to change the world. Over generations, humanity has gone from just another mammal to the dominant species on Earth. This wouldn't have been possible without automation - tasks being completed without the need for humans to exert energy. More recently in our history, humanity has become troublingly reliant on automation. Most services are available online now; booking a flight or hotel, ordering food, shopping, even education/tutoring can be done with little, if any, human interaction. Rather than chatting with someone when there is an issue, services like Amazon or Bank of America have advanced AI that will chat with you to solve it before an actual human. Whether the result of hubris or progress, the expansion of automation has undoubtedly left a question lingering - should we continue down this path of a machine-driven future? ", '    I find myself most agreeing with a mix between the dystopian and utilitarian views. The efficieny of machines does make them well suited for precise, difficult tasks and repetitive jobs. However, these tasks, once done by humans, will need to be seen in a new light. For example, in grocery stores, most now offer the option between a human clerk or an automated self-check out line. These check out lines, much like automatic assembly lines and "chatbots", were once jobs filled by humans. Automation, while beneficial for efficiency, has contributed to the labor crisis.', '    Where I differ from the dystopian view is that besides a loss of respect or basic courtesy, we also become more anti-social and anxious to interact with other people. Rather than call for information or asking a question to an employee, we can look up information online. As previously mentioned, services often provide chatbots at first to solve issues. While these can be great for frequent or easily solvable issues, chatbots do not provide the same level of support or personability as a human.', '    Despite the benefits of automation, there are multiple issues regarding labor rights, human interaction, and the influence of new technology in long-standing fields of work. It is crucial that humanity comes to a consensus on an appropriate balance between automation and human laborers.']

['The Balance of Automation: Exploring Perspectives on the Replacement of Humans with Machines', '', '\tAutomation, a trend that has gained momentum in recent years, is often seen as a symbol of progress and efficiency. The increasing prevalence of intelligent machines in various aspects of society has raised important questions about the implications of replacing human workers with automation. While the benefits of automation are numerous, it is crucial to consider what may be lost when machines take over tasks that were once performed by humans. This paper will explore the multiple perspectives on the issue of automation and examine the potential consequences of relying on intelligent machines.', '\tFrom a dystopian viewpoint, the replacement of human workers by machines signifies a loss of essential human qualities. The decline of face-to-face interactions and personal engagement in favor of automated systems can erode social skills, empathy, and a sense of community. As machines become more integral to daily tasks, individuals may experience a sense of alienation and disconnection from the world around them, leading to a breakdown in social cohesion and a loss of the human touch that defines our interactions.', '\tIn contrast, the utilitarian perspective emphasizes the practical advantages of automation and the efficiencies that intelligent machines bring to various industries. Machines excel in performing low-skill, repetitive tasks and high-speed, precise jobs with a level of accuracy and productivity that surpasses human capabilities. The utilization of automation in such tasks results in increased productivity, cost savings, and improved quality control, ultimately contributing to economic prosperity and progress.', '\tThe progressive view takes a broader lens on the implications of automation, viewing it as an opportunity to challenge traditional notions of human capabilities. Intelligent machines prompt us to rethink our understanding of consciousness, creativity, and intelligence, pushing both humans and machines towards new, unexplored possibilities. Rather than viewing automation as a threat to humanity, the progressive perspective sees it as a catalyst for innovation and collaboration that can reshape society in profound ways.', '\tOne significant issue stemming from increasing automation is the potential displacement of human workers from their jobs. As machines become more advanced and capable of performing a wide range of tasks, there is a growing fear of job loss and unemployment. Workers in industries heavily reliant on automation may struggle to adapt and find new employment opportunities, exacerbating income inequality and social disparities.', '\tAdditionally, the rise of automation raises concerns about the potential loss of human creativity and intuition. While machines are adept at tasks requiring precision and efficiency, they may lack the ability to think creatively and problem-solve in the same way humans can. Innovation often stems from unique human perspectives and ideas, and it is essential to ensure that automation does not stifle this creative potential, as creativity is central to progress and societal advancement.', '\tFinding a balance between automation and human involvement is crucial to harnessing the benefits of intelligent machines while preserving essential human qualities. By integrating automation in a way that complements, rather than replaces, human capabilities and interactions, society can navigate the challenges and opportunities presented by automation. Striking this balance requires careful consideration of the impact of automation on individuals, communities, and society as a whole, ensuring that technological advancements serve to enhance, rather than diminish, the human experience.', '\tIn conclusion, the issue of automation and the replacement of human workers with intelligent machines is multifaceted and complex, with various perspectives highlighting both the benefits and challenges of this technological shift. While automation offers increased efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also poses risks to social interactions, workforce stability, and human creativity. By critically examining and navigating the implications of automation, society can harness the potential of intelligent machines while preserving the essential qualities that define our humanity. Finding a harmonious balance between automation and humanity is essential for shaping a future where progress is driven by the synergy of human ingenuity and technological advancements.']

['When considering the issue of what is lost when we replace humans with machines, it is important to further define the issue. Humans being replaced by machines could mean a variety of things. Therefore, I will clarify that in this paper, when the topic of humans being replaced with machines is mentioned, it is referring to the idea of automated AI systems handling tasks that are repetitive and do not require any kind of human decision-making. In this context, I would consider that nothing is actually lost in this process as long as the tasks being automated are indeed repetitive and free from the need for any kind of decision-making.', '', 'Instead of focusing on the idea that the machine is now doing a job a human once held, it should be recognized that the human who previously held this position will now be able to enhance the effectiveness of their work by finding employment that is more meaningful instead of redundant, mindless work. This will not only improve the production of most industries but also provide the individual with the opportunity to make a better contribution to their company and society. In turn, this will help counteract the negative effects that their previous type of work had on their mental health. Considering a dystopian point of view on this topic, if someone with this type of thinking were to voice their view, they would probably argue that automation strips humans of their purpose and reduces the value of human labor to mere survival, leaving people without meaningful work. They might suggest that such a shift could lead to widespread unemployment, social unrest, and a loss of personal identity for those who derive a sense of purpose from their work. Such a viewpoint would highlight concerns about increased inequality, where the benefits of automation are concentrated in the hands of those who own the machines, while the displaced workers are left without a clear path forward. This could foster resentment and lead to societal divisions, with the potential for significant social upheaval if a large segment of the population feels left behind by technological progress.', '', 'However, this perspective is often contrasted with more optimistic views that emphasize the potential for humans to adapt and find new, more fulfilling roles in an automated world. The key argument against the dystopian view is that throughout history, technological advances have consistently led to the creation of new industries and jobs that were previously unimaginable. For example, the Industrial Revolution, while initially displacing many manual laborers, eventually led to the creation of entirely new fields of work, improved standards of living, and greater overall societal wealth. In this optimistic view, automation could be seen as an opportunity to reimagine work and redefine what it means to have a fulfilling career. As machines take over the drudgery of repetitive tasks, humans can focus on what makes them uniquely human—creativity, empathy, innovation, and complex problem-solving. The challenge, then, is not to resist automation, but to manage its implementation in a way that ensures the benefits are broadly shared and that workers are supported in transitioning to new roles. Ultimately, the discussion around humans being replaced by machines in repetitive tasks is not just about the efficiency and productivity gains but also about how society chooses to handle the transition and what new opportunities can be created in the wake of these changes.', '']

"]

Exploring the interplay of these contrasting perspectives sheds light on the complex and nuanced nature of the discourse surrounding automation's impact on society.", '', 'The ongoing debate surrounding the replacement of human workers with machines encompasses a myriad of complexities and nuances, reflecting diverse perspectives on the societal, economic, and cultural implications of automation. While valid concerns exist regarding the potential loss of human connections and creativity, it is crucial not to overlook the efficiencies and progress facilitated by automation. As we navigate this evolving landscape, striking a delicate balance between technological advancements and the preservation of essential human traits becomes paramount to ensure a sustainable and inclusive future for all.']

["Throughout history, technology has changed the job market. Think about the industrial revolution and how machines replaced some jobs but created new ones. The same is happening now with automation and artificial intelligence. Some people worry that technology will take away all our jobs. But history shows us that when jobs disappear, new ones pop up. For example, as more machines did manufacturing work, the need for computer and data experts grew. Instead of being scared of losing jobs, we should see technology as a chance to learn new skills and find new opportunities. By adapting to new automation, we can create better jobs for ourselves.So percpective is simply being overly paranoid and dramatic. Humans have always adapted and make use of new inventions. As long as we keep learning and growing, we can thrive in a world with automation and AI. It's just another chapter in our story of progress."]

['\tI think that automation has both pros and cons. Automation allows us to progress forward as a society by taking over repetitive and high precision tasks, allowing humans to focus on other pursuits. However, allowing machines to take over so many aspects of our lives can also lead to a regression in the overall social capabilities of humans. For example, many people will order food through an app or website, avoiding the social interaction associated with ordering food. While this is very convenient, it also leads to many people feeling anxious when ordering in person. ', '', '\tMy view is a combination of the utilitarian and dystopian views. I agree with the utilitarian view in that automation leads to a more progressive world, but that world also comes with drawbacks. The drawbacks are described in the dystopian view as losing part of our own humanity. While I think "losing part of our own humanity" is probably an extreme view, machines are definitely changing the way humans interact with one another.  ']

['\tAutomation can have both positive and negative impacts on society. On one hand, automation can greatly benefit society by freeing up humans from tedious tasks, allowing them to focus on more complex endeavors. This can lead to increased efficiency, productivity, and innovation in various industries.', '', '\tHowever, the downside of automation lies in the potential job losses it can create. As automation technology advances, many low-skilled and routine jobs are being replaced, leading to mass layoffs and economic uncertainty for many workers. This can understandably cause feelings of discontent and fear among those whose livelihoods are threatened by automation.', '', '\tTo address these challenges, it is crucial to implement measures that support workers in transitioning to new industries or roles. This could involve investing in retraining programs, providing financial assistance, or creating policies that promote job creation in less automated sectors. Additionally, ethical considerations must be taken into account to ensure that automation is used responsibly, with proper regulations in place to safeguard data privacy and prevent algorithmic biases.', '', '\tBy delving deeper into these complexities, we can explore how to strike a balance between leveraging the benefits of automation for societal advancement while mitigating its negative impacts on the workforce. This holistic approach can help pave the way for a more sustainable and equitable integration of automation in our society.']

['The idea of machines taking over human jobs and tasks has been a topic that has been popular since the inception of the first computer. The topic has only skyrocketed ever since the introduction of Large-Language-Models being released to the public by companies like OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft. Some may take the dystopian perspective, where they argue that replacement of humans for everyday tasks by machines would result in our basic humanity being stripped from us as a society. Another person may take a utilitarian perspective where they believe these machines will be able to eliminate the low-skill and repetitive jobs, leading to a progressive world where more people will be able to focus on more creative and high-skilled tasks. The final perspective I will present to you is the progressive view of automation. The progressive view believes that humans and machines will be pushed to new unimagined possibilities. The three perspective I just mentioned each carry their own validity and can be argued by experts and we would probably still all have differing opinions. ', '', 'The perspective I most align with is the dystopian view and here\'s why. By removing the everyday tasks away from us humans and pawning them off to machines will negatively impact society. Even before A.I. and automation was widely known, from when technology and the internet became a norm in every household, humans were moving closer and closer toward reclusion and isolation. It has only ramped up with the introduction of social media to society. Taking these everyday tasks away from people, even if they are low-skilled jobs, will cause irrepairable damages to people psyches. I believe that if you take low-skilled jobs from people, those people will lose their purpose and motivation. Many people are geneuninely not interested in going to college or having big dreams. Some people are perfectly content just getting by. When you take away people\'s methods of "getting by" and try to change the way they want to live their lives is when there is problems in society.', '', 'The debate surrounding automation and the replacement of humans with machines is multifaceted and complex. While some may foresee a future of unprecedented progress and collaboration between humans and intelligent machines, others raise valid concerns about the potential loss of human connection, purpose, and well-being in a society increasingly reliant on automation.By examining the perspectives presented and engaging in thoughtful dialogue and action, we can shape a future where technology complements rather than dominates our humanity.', '']

['I believe that while automation brings efficiency and progress, it also leads to the loss of important human qualities. The personal touch, emotional connection, and creativity that humans offer cannot be fully replicated by machines. Additionally, job displacement due to automation can result in economic disparities and challenges for affected individuals.', '', 'When comparing my perspective to the utilitarian view, it is evident that both acknowledge the benefits of automation for efficiency and prosperity. However, my focus remains on the human aspect and the potential drawbacks of replacing humans with machines, emphasizing the impact on workers and the significance of human qualities in various aspects of life. This underscores the need for a delicate balance between technological advancements and preserving human values and well-being.']

["\tAs the development of technology advances, the society we live in becomes more and more automated. With this automation brings both benefits and drawbacks for us in many ways. There is a clear economic advantage through automation, but there may be implications for many aspects of a person's financial, social, and psychological life.", '    The automation of repetitive tasks in the workforce has a few major advantages: efficiency, accuracy, and reduced cost of labor, as well as removing humans from potentially dangerous lives in a factory. Machines that can repeat the exact same task many times quickly, without becoming tired, and always in the exact same way allows for the mass production of goods that was not previously achievable. With the advent of AI this advantage only grows, allowing machines to begin to even do jobs that are not repetitive. This includes making decisions to reduce errors and improve safety and efficiency with regards to the processes of creating goods, rather than simply performing the manual labor. AI even allows humans to interact with machines as though they were human. ', '    While these benefits seem great, there are also drawbacks to adding machines to the workforce. One of the most important drawbacks is the impact on employment. Ever since the first addition of machines to assembly lines the problem of employment has been contentious. When a machine takes a job that is traditionally done by a human, the people who make their living with that job tend to experience displacement. This leads to those individuals having economic insecurity and an increase in unemployment and economic inequality in our society. Another major drawback is the effect on the psyche of those in society. Feelings of isolation and disconnection may be brought about as AI is used more and human interaction is needed less. The loss of the human soul in our daily lives can be very damaging to how we see and interact with the world.', '    This view that I hold is a utilitarian view, weighing the benefits and costs of the introduction of machines into the workforce, and the application of AI to increasing the capacity of machines to perform jobs. While I believe that there is great potential for improved production through the use of AI, in the wrong hands and without deliberate caution, the state of our society could deteriorate very quickly.']

['The quick growth of intelligent machines creates ethical dilemmas in the use and misuse of this powerful technology. This issue prompts us to consider the implications of relying on machines for tasks that were once performed by human workers, as well as the broader implications for our interactions, values, and capabilities. In this context, three distinct perspectives emerge: the dystopian view, which emphasizes the loss of our humanity; the utilitarian view, which highlights the efficiency and prosperity brought by machines; and the progressive view, which sees the rise of intelligent machines as a catalyst for new possibilities for both humans and technology. All of these differing prespective are strong arugments and we will examine two of them here.', '', 'My perspective on the issue is that there is a lot to be gained with advancements in AI. The growth of AI can help with small-scale repetitive tasks as well as complicated tasks when using specialized AI. Both of these would increase innovation and technology as a whole. This aligns most with the second perspective. ', '', 'However, a slight difference between my perspective and the utilitarian view may be found in the potential implications for human workers. While I emphasize the overall benefits and advancements that AI can bring, the utilitarian view may downplay the  potential negative consequences for human employment. I do not believe that the growth of AI would help all jobs. This would result in the growth of high skill-level jobs while lower skill-level jobs would take a large hit. This has been seen in the automation of factories.', '', 'In conclusion, while different perspectives, such as the dystopian view, utilitarian view, and progressive view, offer valuable insights into the impacts of AI technology, it is essential to recognize the multifaceted nature of this issue. My perspective aligns with the utilitarian view in acknowledging the benefits and advancements that AI can bring, particularly in enhancing efficiency and innovation. However, my recognition of the potential negative consequences for human workers, particularly in lower skill-level jobs, sets my viewpoint apart from a purely utilitarian perspective. Only through careful examination and thoughtful consideration can we harness the potential of intelligent machines while mitigating the challenges they may pose.']

['Within recent years, the use of automation has increased drastically and is now being integrated into various aspects of everyday life. However, this shift from humans performing tasks to machines performing tasks has sparked a debate about the ethical and practical implications of automation, raising questions about the potential for machines to replace humans in certain roles.', '', 'The utilitarian perspective emphasizes the benefits of automation in enhancing productivity and freeing up individuals from mundane and repetitive tasks. By delegating these tasks to machines, individuals can redirect their focus towards more meaningful and skill-enhancing opportunities that would otherwise not be feasible without automation.', '', 'Furthermore, proponents of the utilitarian view argue that machines outperform humans in low-skill jobs, as they are capable of working at a faster pace and with greater precision. Machines do not require breaks and can maintain consistency in performing repetitive tasks, leading to increased efficiency and quality of work compared to human labor.', '', 'However, not everyone perceives automation as a purely beneficial development; the dystopian perspective offers a contrasting viewpoint. According to this perspective, the increasing reliance on machines to perform tasks previously undertaken by humans is viewed as a threat to our sense of humanity. The dystopian view posits that as machines replace humans in various roles, there is a gradual erosion of meaningful human-to-human interactions. The loss of these interpersonal connections is seen as a potential consequence of excessive automation, leading to a detachment from basic social values such as courtesy, respect, and empathy in everyday interactions.', '', 'In conclusion, the debate surrounding the integration of automation into our daily lives underscores the complexities and nuances of this technological advancement. While the utilitarian perspective highlights the benefits of increased productivity and efficiency that automation offers, the dystopian perspective raises valid concerns about the potential loss of human connection and values in a world increasingly dominated by machines.', '']

['One of the main things that is lost when we replace humans with machines is the human element. Machines lack empathy, creativity, and critical thinking skills that humans possess. They are programmed to perform specific tasks and are unable to provide the same level of personalized care or understanding that a human can provide. This can lead to a decrease in customer satisfaction and overall quality of service.', '', 'Additionally, when jobs are automated, there is a risk of widespread unemployment and job loss. Many industries have already seen a decrease in job opportunities due to automation, and this trend is likely to continue as technology advances. This can lead to economic instability, as displaced workers struggle to find new employment opportunities.', '', 'Furthermore, relying too heavily on automation can lead to a loss of skills and knowledge among the human workforce. When tasks are automated, workers may not have the opportunity to develop important skills or gain valuable experience in their field. This can have long-term consequences for the workforce as a whole.', '', 'Overall, while automation can offer many benefits in terms of efficiency and productivity, it is important to consider the implications and potential drawbacks of replacing humans with machines. Finding a balance between automation and human involvement is key to ensuring that we preserve the unique contributions that humans can make in various industries.']

["Without technology, we don't know what sets humans apart from other species. The crux of what we refer to when asked about what sets us apart from other animals is our intellect. That said, how do we demonstrate such intelligence without technology? Any way that we care for each other or even other species is helped by technology. My view aligns best with the Progressive view. There will always be tasks that are low-skill and repetitive, and it's up to us to create the technology to increase the efficiency for such tasks. ", '', "When we replace humans with machines, we lose the aspect of human encounters whenever we see a need for a task to be done. This, however, is not always a bad thing. There may be less of a need for human interaction, but we can't deny that we save the well-being of the person doing the task when we automate the job. This is partially why I disagree with the Dystopian view. Although we lose the necessity for basic courtesy, respect, and tolerance of other people in what would be a daily human encounter, that should not be a reason that people should continue to engage in ineffcient, monotinous work. We may be social animals by nature, but it is also in our nature to adapt to the cirucmstances as they come up.", '', "Being able to efficiently do every task that comes up is a sign that we are succeeding at attaining a prosperous world. This is why I don't believe that the Progressive view and the Utilitarian view are mutually exclusive. I believe both. We need to be able to figure out how to optimize efficiency and effectiveness of tasks. If we're able to do so, we have succeeded. However, we also have a need to figure out how we as humans fit into the equation. Hence, we are forced to figure out what humans can be, yet another form of adaptation."]

", '', 'The advancement of intelligent machines has revolutionized industries by enhancing productivity, streamlining processes, and improving precision in tasks. ', '', 'While the benefits of intelligent machines are evident, their widespread integration also presents notable drawbacks that must be carefully considered. ', '', 'The societal implications of integrating intelligent machines into various aspects of life warrants thorough examination. ', '', 'The integration of intelligent machines in modern society underscores the intricate balance between technological advance ment and human values. ']

["I believe that automation is a tool that is overall good for society. Unlike AI, which has been faced with far more scrutiny and controversy in the past couple of years, automated machines are involved in completing simple, repetitive tasks and as a result are much easier to control. Furthermore, since the tasks in question aren't overly significant or complicated, there is no risk of machines replacing the majority or even a good amount of human jobs. Of course, there is always an argument that the existence of automation leads to less jobs, but the skill level of these activities can be put to use in other areas of work, such as manual labor or jobs in the hospitality industry. I agree with the statement that it allows both humans and machines to evolve."]

['A machine is a mechanical or electrical device that accomplishes specific tasks by harnessing power from sources such as electricity, steam, or fuel. People commonly refer to machines as their car, dishwasher, or computer. However, modern machines are evolving to be closely allied with automation and robotics. Nowadays, a machine must be complemented by its software counterpart to operate efficiently. For example, a self-checkout machine at a grocery store scans products and uses software to verify the items scanned and calculate the total. The transition from hardware-only machines to a fusion of hardware and software is a recent development.', '', 'Society heavily relies on machines for its functioning today. Assembly lines worldwide are predominantly operated by machines, especially robots assembling components of electronics like iPhones, cars, and computers. This prompts the question of machines potentially supplanting many human roles in production.', '', 'The inevitability of machines taking over is apparent. Companies prefer investing in machines once rather than paying salaries to numerous employees over time. Machines offer perpetual operation, lower costs, flexibility, and require no wages. Therefore, due to these significant advantages, the proliferation of machines worldwide is guaranteed.', '', 'I believe that the rise of machines is a positive development. It accelerates production globally, enabling more goods to be manufactured and sold, thereby boosting the global economy. I align with the perspective that considers machines beneficial for executing repetitive tasks swiftly. It is unfortunate that this progress comes at the expense of humans losing their jobs.']

['\tAutomation can be seen as a sign of progress or as a loss in humanity. While automation has made low-skill and high-speed jobs more efficient, these jobs were traditionally held by humans. Replacing these human jobs with machines causes higher unemployment and a decrease in human interaction. The drawbacks of automation cause many to fear automation; however, automation challenges what it means to be human. With an open mind, humanity can reach unimaginable possibilities with the use of automation. ', '\tOne of the best uses of automation to reach unimaginable possibilities is increasing productivity. Automation has resulted in an increase in productivity across the world. For example, automation has contributed to progress in the manufacturing industry. Automation technologies such as robotics and automated assembly lines have significantly improved efficiency, accuracy, and productivity in manufacturing processes. By automating repetitive tasks, manufacturers can produce goods at a faster rate with fewer errors, leading to cost savings and increased output. This increased efficiency allows companies to meet customer demands more quickly and compete in the global market, ultimately driving economic growth and progress in the industry. While the dystopian view of automation would likely point out that automation in the United States has affected approximately 25% of jobs, according to a study by the Brookings Institution, with certain industries experiencing higher rates of job displacement than others, it is important to note that automation also creates new job opportunities in emerging industries and sectors. In addition to creating new jobs, as automation becomes more and more sophisticated, what is now considered impossible might become second nature. For example, automation in healthcare could lead to AI-powered diagnostic tools that can analyze patient data and medical images quickly and accurately, aiding in the early detection and diagnosis of diseases. Additionally, robots could assist in surgical procedures, offering precision and efficiency in complex surgeries.', '    New and innovative ideas can be terrifying at first simply because they have never been attempted before. Automation is the newest innovation that many people fear, but as with any new idea, stepping past the initial fear can lead to a brighter future.']
